chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Muhrim (one in Ihram) may divorce [his wife] and may marry [again].'
Then the Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: 'And when the Muhrim dies, he is washed like the washing of the Muhrim, except that perfume is not brought near him.'

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: The Muhrim (one in the state of Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of marriage, divorce, and ritual washing for a person in Ihram upon death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the state of Ihram does not restrict the muhrim's capacity for marriage or divorce, distinguishing the ritual sanctity from civil legal status. It further details the post-mortem rites, specifying that while the body is washed according to standard procedure, perfume is not applied to the corpse, preserving the purity of the Ihram state even in death. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the continuity of personal status laws during the Hajj or Umrah pilgrimage.
